- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at 10–15% below true peak.
- If supply net is strongly bearish (net < -20) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside; add 3–8% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.67); model often fails to revert; adjust forecast to align with 14–18 day moving average.
- When official events are frequent (≥20 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model often fails to capture volatility; add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast range.
